title: Perceptron and Artificial Neurons
overview: A neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias and passes it through a nonlinearity. The perceptron is the simplest case and the building block of every deep network.
objectives: Compute the output of a single artificial neuron
Explain why a single neuron only learns linear boundaries

method.title: Weighted sum
method.body: The pre-activation is z = w.x + b, a linear function of the inputs.

method.title: Step activation
method.body: The classic perceptron outputs 1 if z >= 0 and 0 otherwise.

method.title: Learning rule
method.body: On a mistake, move the weights by lr * (y - y_hat) * x so the example moves toward the correct side.

method.title: Linear limit
method.body: A single neuron cannot represent XOR because the classes are not linearly separable.

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[0,0],[0,1],[1,0],[1,1]])
y = np.array([0,0,0,1])  # AND gate
w = np.zeros(2); b = 0.0; lr = 0.1
for epoch in range(10):
    for xi, yi in zip(X, y):
        pred = 1 if xi @ w + b >= 0 else 0
        w += lr * (yi - pred) * xi
        b += lr * (yi - pred)
print("weights", np.round(w, 2), "bias", round(b, 2))
print("predictions", [1 if xi @ w + b >= 0 else 0 for xi in X])
